title: Grateful Dead Live at Boston Music Hall on 1972-09-16

ai_review.summary: Decent soundboard capture of a high‑energy early‑70s set with smoking Bird Song, Dark Star > Brokedown Palace and some of Jerry’s best vocals.
ai_review.review: The show is praised for its big‑number peaks – Bird Song, Morning Dew, Playin', and an expansive Dark Star that rolls into Brokedown Palace – plus a notably strong vocal performance from Garcia. The recording is a partial soundboard mix that is listenable but suffers from a thin low end and occasional audience chatter.

ai_rating.rationale: Strong musical performance (high energy, standout jams) weighted heavily; recording is decent but bass‑thin, lowering the overall score slightly.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Partial soundboard with noticeably low bass and some audience clapping/talk; overall clear enough to enjoy but lacks full depth.

show_quality.setlist_flow: Typical early‑70s Dead set with big‑number jams and a guest keyboard appearance that adds texture; the energy builds through the first half and peaks in the second set.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Garcia’s vocals are highlighted as some of his best from this period, with strong singing on Dew, Dark Star and Brokedown Palace.
band_member_comments.Phil: Bass is thin in the recording, but reviewers note Phil drives the jams (Playin', Dark Star) despite the lack of low‑end presence.
band_member_comments.Keys: Guest Ned Lagin adds Wurlitzer electric piano and wah‑wah on Dark Star > Brokedown Palace; Keith Godchaux is implied on acoustic piano.
